messages:
maya: quick Q — working through the prefix cache contract. Question: when we rotate the prefix key encoding (v1 -> v2), do we guarantee server will accept both encodings in parallel for 1 week? Also how do we signal a cache HIT vs a prefix-only match? Trying to write the API tests.
alex: short answer: yes, accept both for a grace period. but we need a clear header for the hit type. proposal: `x-prefix-cache: hit:v2` or `x-prefix-cache: hit:v1` and `x-prefix-prefetch: true` for prefetch-only. Thoughts?
sam: prefer boolean headers rather than freeform strings. e.g., `x-prefix-cache-hit: true` and `x-prefix-cache-version: v2`. easier for metrics.
jordan: +1 to separate fields. also clarify difference between full response cache hit (full response reused) vs prefix-suffix KV hit (we only had KV cached for the prefix). Maybe `x-cache-scope: full|prefix`?
ciara: from infra: don't add too many headers. we already have `x-cache-status` used by CDN. if we add `x-prefix-cache-hit` and `x-prefix-cache-ver` that's two, ok. avoid freeform `x-prefix-cache`.
maya: ok so concrete: `x-prefix-cache-hit: true|false`, `x-prefix-cache-version: v1|v2`, `x-prefix-cache-scope: full|prefix`. Also include `cache-control` semantics for client: if client sends `cache-control: no-cache` we should bypass prefix cache entirely. Is that the expected behavior?
alex: yes, no-cache should bypass. but we need to document that `max-age=0` is not the same as no-cache for us because we use prefix-level TTL. propose treat `no-cache` and `no-store` as bypass, `max-age=0` still consults cache but may be considered stale -> we can return stale+revalidate behavior.
sam: need to document invalidation contract: POST /invalidate-prefix accepts list of prefix IDs or regex, returns 202 accepted and emits an invalidation-event to the mesh.
jordan: also: when a model changes (e.g., decoder params or tokenizer) we must evict prefix cache for model+version. add `x-prefix-cache-key` scheme: `model:version:prompthash:encoding:v{N}`
ciara: ops note: we'll add a rolling evict job for model rollouts and make invalidation asynchronous. SLA: invalidation should reach all nodes within 90s in normal conditions.
maya: for compatibility: plan is to accept old key encodings for reads for 7 days, write new encoding only. after 7 days we reject legacy reads. add a canary on dedicated clusters for 48h.
alex: tests to add:
- client sends `cache-control: no-cache` -> server bypasses cache
- `x-prefix-cache-hit` present when response reused
- reads accept v1 for 7d while writes always v2
- invalidation endpoint returns 202 and emits event
- model version rollouts cause evict events

sam: pinging @eng-oncall and @devex to confirm observability hooks (traces + metric labels). we need `prefix_cache.hit` and `prefix_cache.scope` tags.
ciara: deploybot: rolling canary scheduled for 03/20 08:00 UTC. :rocket:
deploybot: Canary deploy created: canary-ppcache-20260320. monitoring alerts: prefix_cache_failure_rate > 1% -> rollback.
maya: ok I will update the API doc and send a PR for the test harness. putting action items:
- maya: update API docs + schema PR (in 2d)
- alex: add header parsing + metrics (in 3d)
- sam: add unit/integration tests to eval harness
- ciara: schedule invalidation rollout + ops runbook

jordan: one last nit — for clients that proxy through CDNs, call out that `x-prefix-cache-*` headers may be stripped; recommend using `Cache-Control` + token-level idempotency to detect hits. add to docs.
maya: thanks all. if no objections I'll mark as accepted in 24h and cut the PR.
alex: lgtm :+1:
sam: lgtm
ciara: sounds good
jordan: ok
